newsitem.title: UK: Israel says Britain is big military customer.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Britain is big military customer.

text.p: Britain has bought large amounts of Israeli military equipment since lifting an embargo on arms dealing with the Jewish state, an official accompanying Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on his visit to Britain said.
"I don't know if you are aware but we also have defence coooperation in acquisitions," the senior official said on Tuesday after Netanyahu met Prime Minister John Major.
"Britain has bought from us hundreds of million of dollars (in defence equipment) since the lifting of the embargo 18 months ago," he added without giving details.
He said Israel was also interested in buying British defence equipment but did not specify any shopping lists.
The official said total Israeli-British trade topped $3 billion and that Netanyahu and Major spoke about increasing the figure significantly.
Israel expects to export an estimated 850 million pounds' worth of goods ($1.3 billion) to Britain in 1996 and import $1.4 million pounds' worth ($2.1 million) of British goods this year.

Netanyahu is on his first European diplomatic tour since taking office in June. He arrived in Britain for talks with Major on Tuesday and will travel to Paris on Wednesday for meetings with President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe before going to Bonn on Thursday to meet Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
